result.rule: Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use an interrupting event-subprocess start when the parent scope stops; use non-interrupting only when the parent continues.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.

For each halting condition, give its branch the actions the description states for that condition (for example, notifying a party), then connect that branch to its own explicit end event. Do not leave the halting branch without an end event, so the process always has at least one end event.

When the description says that a step or the whole process concludes only when a time period ends: Model the wait for the end of that time period as an intermediate catch event (a timer event) placed on the flow before the end event, not as a task. Keep the end event for the terminal outcome.

When the description says that a participant remains idle until a stated condition holds, such as its turn being reached, before the next step can begin, and this idle period is not a message being sent or received: Model the idle period as an intermediate catch event in the sequence flow between the step before it and the step after it, and name the event after the condition that ends the idle period. Do not model the idle period as a task, because a task represents work the participant performs, and an idle period contains no work.

When The description states that a party performs an action of its own (for example, a customer giving feedback after a case is closed) and names no message, timer, or condition that the process waits for.: Model that stated action as a task that represents the performed work, placed in the order the description gives. Do not model it as an intermediate catch event, because a catch event represents an occurrence the process waits for. Use a catch event only when the description says the process waits for an external occurrence.
